chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and others from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Hammam said:

I heard al-Rida’ (peace be upon him) saying: 'The slave is returned due to the happenings of the year, such as madness, leprosy, and vitiligo.' We asked, 'How is the return due to the happenings of the year?' He said, 'This is the beginning of the year. If you buy a slave with any of these traits, between you and Dhu al-Hijjah, you can return him to his owner.' Muhammad ibn Ali then asked, 'Is runaway status included in this?' He said, 'Runaway status is not included, unless proof is presented that he was a runaway while with the owner.' It is also narrated from Yunus that the warranty period for madness, leprosy, and vitiligo is one year. And al-Washsha’ narrated that the warranty period for madness alone is one year.

key_terms.أَحْدَاثِ السَّنَةِ: Happenings/events of the year (referring to onset of defects)
key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions and time limits for returning a slave due to defects in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the 'Ayyam al-Nuqs' (days of defects) warranty in Shia jurisprudence, granting the buyer a one-year period to inspect for latent conditions like madness, leprosy, or vitiligo. It specifically clarifies the distinction between inherent defects and behavioral traits, noting that 'runaway' status (al-ibaq) requires independent proof of pre-existing condition rather than being an automatic defect. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring buyers are protected against hidden flaws.

en.sarwar: 17. Muhammad ibn Yahya and others have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from abu Hammam who has said the following:

“I once heard al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Slaves, because of the happenings of the year are returned, such as madness, leprosy and Bars (leprosy).’ We then asked, ‘How is the return because of the happenings of the year?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘This is the beginning of the year. If you buy a slave with any of these things up to the month of Dhu al-Hajjah you can return to the owner.’ Muhammad ibn Ali then asked, ‘Are runaway slaves subject to this condition?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Runaway is not so treated, unless proof is presented that he was a runaway with the owner.’ It is narrated from Yunus also that the time for return in the case of madness, leprosy and Bars (leprosy) is one year. Al- Washsha’ has narrated that time for returning due to madness alone is one year.”
